paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God was working on BOTH ends of the road before anybody knew there was a road. He sent an angel to Cornelius in Caesarea, and He gave Peter a vision on a roof in Joppa. Then the Spirit told Peter, "Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them" (Acts 10:20). Two men, two cities, one God who had the whole thing lined up like a perfect batch.

Now look at what Peter was up against. God said, "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean" (Acts 10:15), and Peter had spent his whole life with the law saying otherwise (Leviticus 11). That's a lot to wrap your head around, and the text says he was "puzzling over the meaning of the vision" (Acts 10:17). I think that's the honest part, friend: when God says something that doesn't fit what you've always known, you can stop and puzzle, and still be ready to listen.

And here's what it means for you, baker. Cornelius prayed and gave to the poor, and the angel said those gifts had ascended "as a memorial offering before God" (Acts 10:4). God noticed him. Peter was still puzzling when the Spirit spoke, and he listened and went down to the men (Acts 10:19-21), so keep listening to God, friend, and be ready to say yes like Peter.
